mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate signals an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives up stock prices and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index experiences a decline in value over the next 20 trading days following a decrease in the federal funds rate, or the correlation between the federal funds rate and S&P 500 returns is found to be insignificant.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 10% triggers a signal that the economy is entering a recession, leading to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index experiences a significant increase in value over the next 60 trading days following an increase in the unemployment rate above 10%, or the unemployment rate is found to be an insignificant predictor of S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts, as measured by the HOUST series, signals an increase in demand for housing and related goods, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index experiences a decline in value over the next 5 trading days following an increase in housing starts, or the correlation between housing starts and S&P 500 returns is found to be insignificant.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production, as measured by the INDPRO series, signals an increase in supply and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index experiences a decline in value over the next 20 trading days following an increase in industrial production, or the correlation between industrial production and S&P 500 returns is found to be insignificant.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the federal funds rate and the consumer price index signals an increase in inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days when the federal funds rate is below 1% and the consumer price index is above 2%.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index experiences a significant increase in value over the next 60 trading days when the federal funds rate is below 1% and the consumer price index is above 2%, or the interaction between the federal funds rate and the consumer price index is found to be an insignificant predictor of S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the unemployment rate and the number of employees in the nonfarm payroll sector signals an increase in labor market tightness, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days when the unemployment rate is below 5% and the number of employees is above 130 million.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index experiences a decline in value over the next 20 trading days when the unemployment rate is below 5% and the number of employees is above 130 million, or the interaction between the unemployment rate and the number of employees is found to be an insignificant predictor of S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the GDP growth rate, as measured by the GDPC1 series, signals a decrease in demand and economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index experiences a significant increase in value over the next 60 trading days following a decrease in the GDP growth rate, or the GDP growth rate is found to be an insignificant predictor of S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between industrial production and housing starts signals an increase in supply and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days when industrial production is above 100 and housing starts are above 500,000.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 index experiences a decline in value over the next 5 trading days when industrial production is above 100 and housing starts are above 500,000, or the interaction between industrial production and housing starts is found to be an insignificant predictor of S&P 500 returns.
